images.caption: View of South Africa taken during ISS Expedition 6, which shows the Garden Route District of the Western Cape, a province of South Africa. The view covers the region from about the hamlet of Vermaaklikheid at far left, to the city of George on the far right. George, Western Cape, is the second-largest city in the province and serves as the administrative and commercial hub for the Garden Route region. The green slopes of two major mountain ranges of the Cape Fold Belt are visible as a dark band dividing the landscape. These are the Langeberg at left, and the Outeniqua Mountains to the right. The region in their rain shadow is known as Cannaland, which constitutes the southwestern part of the Little Karoo. The Cannaland basin, eastern parts of the Langeberg and northern slopes of the Outeniqua are drained by the Gourits River and its numerous tributaries. The Gourits, a haven for native aquatic life, cuts through Die Poort, a defile in the Langeberg, to reach the Indian Ocean near Vleesbaai.

images.filename: The coastal region of South Africa (iss071e580719).jpg
images.caption: iss071e580719 (Aug. 30, 2024) — The coastal plains and Cape Fold Belt of the Western Cape, South Africa, in winter, with Cape Town and False Bay situated at the top right of the image. These are pictured from the International Space Station as it orbited 265 miles above. In the foreground the green wheat producing region of the Swartland is evident, and beyond the Cape Fold Belt, that of the Overberg.  Cape Agulhas near the top border, defines the meeting point of the Indian and South Atlantic Oceans, while a billow of cumulus cloud at top right reveals air convection over the warm Agulhas Current. Sediment plumes are visible at the mouths of the Berg River in St Helena Bay at bottom left, and the Diep River in Table Bay. Cape Columbine, named for one of many local shipwrecks, is near the southern boundary of the image. The cold and nutrient-rich Benguela Current sweeps northward past this perilous point, as the sediment plumes also indicate. The Cape of Good Hope juts out into the South Atlantic on the far right. The vicinities of these three capes are protected by a nature reserve and two national parks respectively.
images.alt: iss071e580719 (Aug. 30, 2024) — The coastal plains and Cape Fold Belt of the Western Cape, South Africa, in winter, with Cape Town and False Bay situated at the top right of the image. images.filename: The coastal region of South Africa (iss071e580719), Breede River Valley.jpg
images.caption: iss071e580719 (Aug. 30, 2024) — The Breede River Valley in the Western Cape, South Africa, in winter, pictured from the International Space Station as it orbited 265 miles above. The Breede River has its source at Michell's Pass, north of Worcester. Southwards of the town it enters the valley wedged between the Langeberg and Riviersonderend Mountains, before it enters the Overberg, the green crop fields of which can be seen beyond the Cape Fold Belt.
images.alt: iss071e580719 (Aug. 30, 2024) — The Breede River Valley in the Western Cape, South Africa, in winter, pictured from the International Space Station as it orbited 265 miles above. The Breede River has its source at Michell's Pass, north of Worcester.
